- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.3), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in subsequent days; apply a 2–5% downward bias to next forecast.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with low sentiment, it overestimates; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 5-day average.
- If model shows strong downward trend with high sentiment, it underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment mismatch”.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if recent 10-day average is > forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with historical mean reversion behavior.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative within 3 days, model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
